mizutani: Baltistan
proposed: the Palola Ṣāhis' kingdom (Palola, Bolor); seat Baltistan or Gilgit, open
basis: all authorities; Himalayan Districts II 1884 reports Chitral (Klaproth) as the other Bolor, which the text's E bearing excludes; hearsay; name: 鉢露羅 = *Palola (p, l), dynastic name of the Palola/Paṭola Ṣāhis of Gilgit (Hatun inscription EI 30; Gilgit colophon); form settled: Palola as a country name in rock inscriptions (von Hinüber 1989 pp. 64-65, Hodar no. 64; 2004 pp. 105-106, nos. 24-27, 鉢露羅 its best Chinese transcription): names the kingdom, not its seat; Ji: 鉢露羅 = Great Bolor (Baltistan), Little Bolor at Gilgit-Yasin; Gilgit 82 km, 24 deg off (data/names/); Kuwayama 2002 pp. 145-146 and 1990 p. 149: 鉢露羅 = Zhimeng's 波倫 = Bolor, reached from Tashkurghan by the Ishkoman or Darkot passes, i.e. Gilgit (5th-c. pilgrims' road; Baltistan not discussed); Neelis 2011 pp. 176-177, 275: Bolor = the Palola Sahi realm (Gilgit), Great Bolor = Baltistan in the 8th c.; no argument against Baltistan for the 7th; Jettmar 1989 pp. XIX, L and 1993 pp. 78-83: seat in Baltistan (Great Palur, Skardu), Gilgit a conquered province, from Huichao and the Tang annals (8th c.); Fussman 1993 pp. 16-17: Skardu unproven without inscriptions there; von Hinüber 2004 pp. 7-8, 56, 69-71: dynasty c. 600-early 8th c., dated royal inscriptions all from the Gilgit valley (Hatun 671, Danyor 687), Tang Great Bolor kings = Palola Sahis, Shigar inscription 6th c. and of another king (not Palola evidence); seat open
